{{Short description|Theorem in probability theory}}
In [[probability theory]], the '''Palm&ndash;Khintchine theorem''', the work of [[Conny Palm]] and [[Aleksandr Khinchin]], expresses that a large number of [[renewal process]]es, not necessarily [[Poisson process|Poissonian]], when combined ("superimposed") will have Poissonian properties.<ref name="heymansobel">{{cite book
|title = Stochastic Models in Operations Research: Stochastic Processes and Operating Characteristics
|author = Daniel P. Heyman, Matthew J. Sobel
|year = 2003
|chapter = 5.8 Superposition of Renewal Processes
}}</ref>

It is used to generalise the behaviour of users or clients in [[queuing theory]]. It is also used in dependability and reliability modelling of computing and [[telecommunications]].

==Theorem==

According to Heyman and Sobel (2003),<ref name="heymansobel"/> the theorem states that the superposition of a large number of independent equilibrium renewal processes, each with a finite intensity, behaves asymptotically like a Poisson process:

Let <math>\{N_i(t),t\geq 0\}, i=1,2,\ldots, m</math> be independent renewal processes and <math>\{N(t),t>0\}</math> be the superposition of these processes. Denote by <math>X_{jm}</math> the time between the first and the second renewal epochs in process <math>j</math>. Define <math>N_{jm}(t)</math> the <math>j</math>th counting process, <math>F_{jm}(t)=P(X_{jm}\leq t)</math> and  <math>\lambda_{jm}=1/(E((X_{jm)}))</math>. 

If the following assumptions hold

1) For all sufficiently large <math>m</math>: <math> \lambda_{1m}+\lambda_{m}+\cdots+\lambda_{mm}=\lambda<\infty </math>

2) Given <math>\varepsilon>0</math>, for every <math>t>0</math> and sufficiently large <math>m</math>: <math>F_{jm}(t)<\varepsilon</math> for all <math>j</math>

then the superposition <math>N_{0m}(t)=N_{1m}(t)+N_{m}(t)+\cdots+N_{mm}(t)</math> of the counting processes approaches a Poisson process as <math>m \to \infty</math>.
